practice_description.medium: Institutional programme: commissioning, R&D, strategic publishing, policy convening
practice_description.practice_summary: Serpentine's Arts Technologies department commissions and produces artworks engaging with advanced technologies (AI, blockchain, video games, life sciences) while publishing the Future Art Ecosystems strategic briefings and operating dedicated R&D labs (Creative AI Lab, Blockchain Lab, Legal Lab, Synthetic Ecologies Lab).
practice_description.methodology: Established in 2014, the programme operates through three interlinked activities: (1) commissioning artworks at the art/technology intersection (Cecile B. Evans, James Bridle, Jenna Sutela, Ian Cheng, Pierre Huyghe, Hito Steyerl, Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst); (2) an R&D Platform with dedicated labs conducting applied research; and (3) Future Art Ecosystems -- annual strategic briefings co-produced with Rival Strategy that convene art, technology, law, policy, and academia. Led by Kay Watson (Head of Arts Technologies) with team including Eva Jager, Victoria Ivanova, Tamar Clarke-Brown, Tommie Introna, Lina Martin-Chan, Vi Trinh, and Ruth Waters.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Serpentine Arts Technologies is the leading institutional programme defining how art institutions engage with advanced technologies. Their Future Art Ecosystems reports provide the strategic and conceptual framework within which A(DAI)'s work sits, and their commissioning of The Call directly produced governance innovations (Data Trust) relevant to A(DAI)'s approach.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Indirectly. Serpentine commissions artworks that function as substrate (The Call's choral AI models, Ian Cheng's simulations), but the programme itself operates as institutional infrastructure rather than producing art directly.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: The FAE reports map relational ecosystems between art, technology, policy, and society. The R&D labs explicitly work across disciplines to produce new relational configurations.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: The programme evolves year-on-year through its FAE publications (each building on prior issues) and its evolving lab structure. FAE4 (Art x Public AI) and FAE5 (Art x Creative R&D) represent the latest iteration.

works.title: Future Art Ecosystems 4: Art x Public AI
works.description: Fourth annual strategic briefing addressing art's role in shaping public AI. Called for artists and institutions to become 'stewards' of data. Developed alongside The Call's Data Trust experiment.
works.relevance: Directly frames the policy and governance context for A(DAI)'s commons-first approach to AI and collective intelligence.

works.title: Future Art Ecosystems 5: Art x Creative R&D
works.description: Fifth publication mapping the creative R&D landscape and recommending how cultural sector, creative industries, academia, and policy can shape it. Celebrates 10 years of Serpentine Arts Technologies.
works.relevance: Provides the institutional and policy framework for positioning A(DAI) as creative R&D infrastructure.

works.title: The Call (Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst commission)
works.description: Major commission at Serpentine North (Oct 2024 - Feb 2025) combining choral AI installation with a pioneering Data Trust governance experiment, co-developed with the FAE team.
works.relevance: Demonstrates Serpentine's capacity to produce artworks that are simultaneously artistic, technological, and governance innovations -- the model for A(DAI)'s approach.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Serpentine Arts Technologies treats institutional infrastructure itself as a creative medium. The FAE reports design protocols for how art institutions should engage with technology. The R&D labs prototype new legal, governance, and technical frameworks. The Data Trust experiment from The Call is a governance protocol produced through artistic commissioning.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Future Art Ecosystems publication series (5 issues, 2020-2025); Creative AI Lab (with King's College London); Blockchain Lab (with Ruth Catlow/Furtherfield); Legal Lab; Synthetic Ecologies Lab; Data Trust experiment (with The Call); Artist Worlds commission series; Creative R&D Working Group (national)

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Strongly commons-oriented. FAE reports are published openly. The programme explicitly advocates for artists and institutions as 'stewards' of data rather than extractors. The Data Trust experiment models collective data governance. The Creative AI Lab and Blockchain Lab research commons-based alternatives. FAE5 recommends equitable value distribution and moving beyond commercial metrics.

governance_model.governance_detail: Operates within Serpentine Galleries' institutional structure. Led by Kay Watson (Head of Arts Technologies) with a dedicated team. R&D labs have their own leads (Ruth Catlow for Blockchain Lab; Mercedes Bunz and Eva Jager for Creative AI Lab). FAE is co-produced with external partner Rival Strategy. Governance innovation is a research output (Data Trust, Blockchain Lab's DAO explorations) rather than the programme's own governance model.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: As a commissioner, Serpentine develops consent frameworks collaboratively with artists. The Data Trust experiment from The Call represents their most advanced consent model. The Blockchain Lab's work with Ruth Catlow explores decentralised consent structures.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Institutional authorship for FAE reports (team-credited). Commissioned artworks are attributed to artists. R&D outputs are collaborative (e.g., Creative AI Lab co-authored with King's College London). The programme positions itself as facilitator rather than sole author.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: The programme produces annual FAE publications, ongoing lab research, and periodic commissions. Each output builds on prior work -- FAE5 explicitly builds on 5 years of FAE and 10 years of Arts Technologies. The programme is designed as permanent institutional infrastructure.

data_materiality.data_sources: Research data from R&D labs, commissioned artwork outputs, FAE report research (interviews, case studies, policy analysis), workshop and convening outputs, Creative AI Lab research datasets.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Institutional research produced through collaborative processes. Commissioned artwork data governed by artist agreements (e.g., Data Trust for The Call). FAE reports are publicly available.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: The Creative AI Lab researches AI/ML systems from artistic and cultural perspectives, including engagement with embedding spaces. Commissioned artists (Herndon/Dryhurst, Ian Cheng) work directly with AI latent spaces.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes. The programme spans visual art, sound, gaming, life sciences, blockchain, and text-based strategic publishing.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Operates across Serpentine's physical galleries (Serpentine North, Serpentine South), online publications (futureartecosystems.org), downloadable games (Artist Worlds), and convening events. The FAE reports function as 'exhibitions' of ideas.

interoperability.composability: Highly composable. FAE reports provide frameworks that other institutions adopt. R&D lab outputs (Data Trust, legal frameworks) are designed to be replicated. The Creative R&D Working Group convenes a national network. Published research is freely accessible.
interoperability.technical_openness: Open. FAE reports are publicly published. Research outputs are shared. The programme explicitly advocates for openness and commons-based approaches.

technical_approach.stack: Institutional infrastructure, academic partnerships (King's College London, Centre for Data Futures), strategic publishing, blockchain prototyping (Tezos), AI/ML research, legal and governance frameworks, data trust infrastructure

network_position.scene_affiliation: London institutional art world, Serpentine Galleries ecosystem, UK cultural policy, academic technology research (King's College London), blockchain/Web3 art (through Blockchain Lab and Ruth Catlow/Furtherfield), international art/technology discourse
network_position.connections: Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst (commissioned artists), Fellowship.xyz (Eva Jager contributes to both), Feral File (parallel digital art platform), KW Institute Berlin (Starmirror), RadicalxChange (Data Trust collaboration), King's College London (Creative AI Lab partner), Rival Strategy (FAE co-producer), Ruth Catlow/Furtherfield (Blockchain Lab), Kulturstiftung des Bundes, Hans Ulrich Obrist (Serpentine artistic director)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Serpentine Arts Technologies provides the institutional and conceptual framework most aligned with A(DAI). Their FAE reports define the discourse A(DAI) operates within. Potential roles: advisory partnership, co-research through Creative AI Lab, Data Trust methodology transfer, policy legitimacy through FAE network, and access to their commissioned artist network. Kay Watson and Eva Jager are key conversation partners.
